subject: Next steps: workload hypotheses & POC traffic roadmap
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Kai Nguyen <kai@novanet.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 26 May 2027 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Next steps: workload hypotheses & POC traffic roadmap

Hi Kai — great call today, thanks for walking us through the integration goals. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can align POC scope and acceptance criteria.

Recap (from our call)
- Primary goal: validate production cost and latency for the inline summarization + search re-ranker flow.
- Key constraint: end-to-end 95th latency target <= 350ms for write-heavy bursts; cost target TBD but needs to be competitive with current infra.

Workload hypotheses we captured
- Steady-state RPS: low single digits (you said ~5–10 rps)
- Burst profile: short spikes to ~100–140 RPS lasting 1–4 minutes for traffic surges
- Typical request token lengths: ~180–260 tokens (median ~210)
- Concurrency: expected active concurrency ~30–50 during peak windows

POC ask / success criteria (proposed)
1) Functional: accuracy parity with baseline for top-3 reranker output (we'll use the eval set you agreed to share).
2) Performance: 95th-token latency under 350ms for steady and burst windows for 95% of samples.
3) Cost: target per-1M-token cost within X% of your current baseline (agree on baseline before run).
4) Ops: ability to run canary model variant and automatic fallback without manual intervention.

Immediate next steps
- I attached a lightweight intake sheet (novanet_workload_intake_v1.xlsx) — please populate the green fields (sample corpus link, exact concurrency plan, any rate-limiting on your side).
- Send a small sample of production traces / representative requests (anonymized) to devops@redwood.com so we can synthesize realistic payloads.
- Confirm timeline: we propose a 2-week evaluation window after ingestion + 5 business days for baseline benchmarking.

Owners
- Redwood AM: Soojin Lee (me) — POC coordination, success criteria signoff
- Redwood Infra: Ben Carter — runtime benchmarks and capacity plan
- Redwood Runtime: Markus Klein — kernel/quantization tuning and canary rollouts
- Novanet: Kai (primary), DevOps (ingest + logs)

If that looks good I can push a formal POC plan and calendar invite tomorrow.

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Account Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Kai Nguyen <kai@novanet.com>

Cc: Novanet DevOps <devops@novanet.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 27 May 2027 09:18:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Next steps: workload hypotheses & POC traffic roadmap

Thanks Soojin — appreciate the clear summary. Confirming the numbers from our side and adding a few clarifications: we populated the intake sheet and attached a small trace extract.

Confirmed/testing numbers
- Steady RPS: 8 rps average (business hours), long tail down to 1–2 rps off-peak.
- Burst: our spikes are tied to batch jobs and external traffic; we see bursts to 120–140 RPS that last 90–240 seconds. These occur ~4–6 times/day during peak season.
- Tokens: median request length ~220 tokens, 90th percentile ~480 (we have some long-form user notes).
- Concurrency: typical active concurrency during peak ~45; rare situations spike to 80 for <30s.

SLOs / constraints
- We care more about 95th latency for the whole pipeline than p50. If you can hit <350ms for 95th in steady and within 500ms during short bursts we should be OK.
- Budget: we need a ballpark for cost per 1M tokens for a sustained trial — please include in the POC plan.

Attachments
- devops_sample_trace.json (anonymized request+timing) — contains timestamped traces and sample payload sizes.

We can start the ingestion window on Monday (31 May) if Redwood can provision a small canary environment by then.

—Kai
Kai Nguyen
Head of Infrastructure, Novanet
[kai@novanet.com]

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Kai Nguyen <kai@novanet.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 11:26:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Next steps: workload hypotheses & POC traffic roadmap

Perfect — thanks for the fast turnaround, Kai. Based on the trace and numbers here's a concrete POC plan and timeline. Please review and confirm (one-line approvals are fine).

POC plan (high level)
- Pre-ingestion (Day -2 to 0): final intake sheet + access to sample corpus and anonymized traces. Redwood to prepare test harness and synthetic workload generator.
- Ingestion & baseline benchmarking (Days 1–5): run a controlled replay of traces at steady-state to establish baseline latency/cost.
- Burst stress validation (Days 6–8): run scheduled burst simulations (short 90–240s spikes) with telemetry collection and fallback behavior testing.
- Evaluation & readout (Days 9–14): analyze outputs against success criteria; produce readout deck + recommendations.

Deliverables
- Benchmark report (latency percentiles, token-level cost breakdown, tail behavior)
- Canary runbook (how to roll forward/fallback between model variants)
- Gap list and recommended optimizations (batching, cache policies, quantization profile)

Who does what
- Novanet: provide sample corpus + trace access, confirm rate limits, nominate a single point of contact for incident escalation.
- Redwood: provision test environment, run benchmarks, and deliver report.

Timeline
- Proposed start: Mon, 31 May 2027 (ingest + baseline).
- End / readout: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 (two-week evaluation).

Open items for Novanet signoff
- Confirm start date (31 May) or suggest alternatives.
- Sign off on success criteria in the attached poc_success_criteria.md or provide edits.
- Confirm access for Redwood to replay traces (S3 bucket credentials or shared Drive).

If you approve, I'll create a calendar series and load owners + milestones into the shared Drive folder.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this running.

Cheers,
Soojin Lee
Account Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 29 May 2027 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Next steps: workload hypotheses & POC traffic roadmap

Quick infra note (internal) — tagging this here so Markus can pick it up before Monday.

Observations from the sample trace:
- Token distribution confirms long tail; we'll need to preserve KV-cache behavior for summarization to avoid repeated compute on repeated prefixes.
- For the burst profile Kai described, start with batch_size=8 per GPU and aggressive prefix caching. If latency is still above target during 90–240s spikes, we should try: reduce batch_size to 4 for canary variant, enable int8 quantization path, and tune kernel launch for sequence lengths ~480.

Action items
- Markus: prototype a canary config with (batch_size=4, int8, caching=aggressive) and run a synthetic 150 RPS 2-minute spike this weekend in staging. Report perf delta to Soojin by Monday EOD.
- Soojin: include this as an explicit test case in the POC runbook (burst 150 RPS, 120s, monitor 95th latency).

Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
